notes: Harder Pick menus (doc 44 §5.4 item 4), same item schema as pick.json and scored as Pick ('shape'). Every menu has exactly 7 real options plus the escape 'none_fit' (always X). Distractors are near misses that differ from the answer in one decisive detail stated in the request, the option text or the card. Requests are 2-4 sentences and each carries one irrelevant detail. Three items (HM04, HA03, HR04) are planted escapes whose only correct answer is X. Cards restate the rules of the cited Standing Orders entries and research docs, not the item's answer. Ids differ from pick.json's, so seeds and permutations are new. Routing ids are the workflow ids the docs name (docs 21, 38 and 39).

items.request: A crewed truck group has six of its own riflemen riding in the back; they belong to the same group and start In cargo. At the farm the riflemen should climb down, but the driver must stay behind the wheel. The truck is painted in winter camouflage. Which waypoint type goes on this group's route at the farm?

options.label: UNLOAD
options.desc: the group's own passengers dismount; the crew stays aboard; moves on at once

options.label: TR UNLOAD
options.desc: passengers from other groups dismount; finishes when none remain

options.label: GET OUT
options.desc: everyone dismounts, the crew included

options.label: LOAD
options.desc: orders the group's own units into its own vehicles; moves on at once

options.label: GET IN
options.desc: boards the attached vehicle, or the synced other group's transport

options.label: MOVE
options.desc: goes to the spot; finishes on arrival

options.label: HOLD
options.desc: stays at the spot and never finishes; only a Switch trigger moves the group on

items.card: Standing Orders, lifts: UNLOAD makes the group's OWN passengers get out while the crew stays, and moves on at once. TR UNLOAD orders out passengers who belong to OTHER groups and finishes when none remain. GET OUT dismounts everyone, crew included. LOAD orders the group's own units into its own vehicles and does not wait. 'In cargo' seats soldiers in a vehicle of their own group.
items.rationale: The riflemen belong to the truck's own group, so UNLOAD: its own passengers get out and the crew stays. TR UNLOAD affects only other groups' passengers, and GET OUT would take the driver out too.

escape.label: None of these fit
escape.desc: no listed option fits the request

items.request: Squad Bravo has lost its sergeant and two riflemen. At the church it must meet Squad Alpha and carry on as part of Alpha, under Alpha's leader; its waypoint there will be synced to Alpha's waypoint. The church tower has lost its roof. Which waypoint type does BRAVO get at the church?

options.label: JOIN
options.desc: this group merges into the target group

options.label: JOIN AND LEAD
options.desc: the target group merges into this group

options.label: GET IN
options.desc: boards the attached vehicle, or the synced other group's transport

options.label: TALK
options.desc: walks to about 3 m in front of the attached unit; says nothing

options.label: MOVE
options.desc: goes to the spot; finishes on arrival

options.label: HOLD
options.desc: stays at the spot and never finishes; only a Switch trigger moves the group on

options.label: GUARD
options.desc: joins the side's reaction pool, or guards a synced trigger's area; never finishes

items.card: Standing Orders, waypoint types: JOIN merges this group INTO the target group (the attached unit's group, or the other group of a two-group sync). JOIN AND LEAD does the reverse: the target group merges into THIS group. GET IN boards a vehicle. TALK only walks up to the attached unit. HOLD and GUARD never finish.
items.rationale: Bravo is to become part of Alpha under Alpha's leader, so Bravo gets JOIN, which merges it into the synced group. JOIN AND LEAD would pull Alpha into Bravo instead.

items.request: An AI-led East ambush squad lies hidden on the hill above the road; its next waypoint is a SEEK AND DESTROY at the road bend. On the hill it must stay put and move on by itself only once it has made out the West convoy as hostile. The hill has a ruined windmill. Which waypoint type does the squad get on the hill?

options.label: SENTRY
options.desc: watches the area; finishes once an enemy is identified

options.label: HOLD
options.desc: stays at the spot and never finishes; only a Switch trigger moves the group on

options.label: GUARD
options.desc: joins the side's reaction pool, or guards a synced trigger's area; never finishes

options.label: SEEK AND DESTROY
options.desc: searches around the spot; finishes after five empty sweeps in a row

options.label: DESTROY
options.desc: attacks the attached target; unattached, the nearest vehicle within 100 m, of any side

options.label: MOVE
options.desc: goes to the spot; finishes on arrival

options.label: SUPPORT
options.desc: waits as repair, fuel, ammo or medical support; never finishes

items.card: Standing Orders, waypoint types: SENTRY watches its area and finishes when an enemy is identified (never for a player-led group). HOLD, GUARD and SUPPORT never finish by themselves; a Switch trigger moves the group on. Unsynced GUARD groups are sent to threats anywhere the side knows of. SEEK AND DESTROY searches the spot until five sweeps in a row find nothing. An unattached DESTROY attacks the nearest vehicle within 100 m of the spot, of any side.
items.rationale: It must wait on the hill and leave by itself once it identifies the enemy: SENTRY. HOLD needs a Switch trigger, GUARD would be dispatched elsewhere, and the SEEK AND DESTROY in the request is the NEXT waypoint.

escape.desc: no listed option fits the request

items.request: A West patrol starts at the barracks and has three MOVE waypoints: north gate, east tower, south gate. After that it must walk north gate, east tower, south gate again and again, never going back to the barracks. The barracks has a red roof. What should the fourth waypoint be, and where?

options.label: CYCLE on the north gate
options.desc: a CYCLE dropped right on top of waypoint 1

options.label: CYCLE at the barracks
options.desc: a CYCLE dropped beside the leader's start position

options.label: CYCLE beside the south gate
options.desc: a CYCLE dropped next to waypoint 3

options.label: CYCLE beside the east tower
options.desc: a CYCLE dropped next to waypoint 2

options.label: MOVE at the north gate
options.desc: a fourth MOVE waypoint on waypoint 1's spot

options.label: HOLD at the north gate
options.desc: a HOLD waypoint on waypoint 1's spot

options.label: GUARD at the north gate
options.desc: a GUARD waypoint on waypoint 1's spot

items.card: Standing Orders, CYCLE: a CYCLE has no target field. When it becomes current, the group jumps to whichever earlier waypoint lies nearest to where the CYCLE marker was placed; the hidden waypoint 0 at the leader's start position and the waypoint just before the CYCLE are candidates too, and on a tie the earliest wins. MOVE finishes on arrival; HOLD and GUARD never finish.
items.rationale: The loop target is the earlier waypoint nearest to the CYCLE, so it must sit on the north-gate waypoint. Beside the barracks it loops back to the start, beside the east tower it skips the north gate, beside the south gate the group stalls there; MOVE ends the route and HOLD or GUARD never finish.

items.request: A crewed truck must collect a separate infantry squad at the crossroads and must not leave until every man is aboard; then it drives them to the village. The squad's own waypoint at the crossroads is GET IN. The squad carries two machine guns. Which waypoint does the TRUCK get at the crossroads?

options.label: LOAD, synced to the squad's GET IN
options.desc: the transport's pickup waypoint, with a sync line to the passengers' waypoint

options.label: LOAD, no sync
options.desc: the transport's pickup waypoint, with no sync line

options.label: MOVE, no sync
options.desc: drive to the crossroads; no sync line

options.label: HOLD, synced to the squad's GET IN
options.desc: stop at the crossroads for good; sync line to the passengers' waypoint

options.label: LOAD, synced to a Radio Alpha trigger
options.desc: the transport's pickup waypoint, with a sync line to a radio call

options.label: SUPPORT, synced to the squad's GET IN
options.desc: wait at the crossroads as a supply truck; sync line to the passengers' waypoint

options.label: GET IN, synced to the squad's GET IN
options.desc: the truck group itself boards a vehicle; sync line to the passengers' waypoint

items.card: Standing Orders, lifts and syncs: a waypoint with sync lines, once its job is done, waits until every synced partner is ready. A synced GET IN becomes ready only after its group has boarded; a synced trigger becomes ready when it fires. LOAD orders the group's own units into its own vehicles and does not wait by itself; MOVE finishes on arrival. HOLD and SUPPORT never finish. GET IN makes its own group board a vehicle.
items.rationale: The waiting comes from the sync: LOAD synced to the squad's GET IN holds until the squad has boarded, then the truck moves on. Unsynced LOAD or MOVE leaves at once, a sync to a radio trigger waits for the call instead of the boarding, HOLD and SUPPORT never let the truck leave, and GET IN would have the truck group board a vehicle itself. (UNLOAD or TR UNLOAD synced to the GET IN would also hold, since their job ends at once with nobody aboard, so they are not used as distractors.)

items.request: The win trigger is linked to the enemy officer's squad and covers their camp. The mission should be won only when not one man of that squad is left inside the camp, whether they were killed or ran away. The officer smokes a pipe. Which linked activation and presence?

options.label: Whole group, Present
options.desc: fires when every member is inside the area

options.label: Whole group, Not present
options.desc: fires as soon as not every member is inside the area

options.label: Any group member, Present
options.desc: fires when at least one member is inside the area

options.label: Any group member, Not present
options.desc: fires once none of the members is inside the area

options.label: Group leader, Present
options.desc: fires when the current leader is inside the area

options.label: Group leader, Not present
options.desc: fires when the current leader is not inside the area

options.label: Vehicle, Not present
options.desc: fires when the linked soldier himself is outside the area or dead

items.card: Standing Orders, linked triggers: read the labels literally. Whole group + Present: every member inside. Whole group + Not present: fires when at least ONE member is outside. Any group member + Present: any member inside. Any group member + Not present: NO member inside. Group leader tracks only the current leader; Vehicle tracks the linked unit itself. Dead soldiers never count as inside.
items.rationale: 'Not one man left inside' is Any group member, Not present. Whole group, Not present fires as soon as a single member steps out or dies, and Group leader or Vehicle watch one man only.

items.request: Evacuation trigger, West Present over the landing zone: the helicopter may be called only after the squad has held the zone for a full 45 seconds, exactly, not a random wait. If the zone is empty even for a moment, the 45 seconds must start again from zero. The zone is marked with green smoke. Which timer setting?

options.label: Timeout, min 45 / mid 45 / max 45
options.desc: the condition must stay true for the whole delay, or the clock resets

options.label: Timeout, min 30 / mid 45 / max 60
options.desc: the condition must stay true for the whole delay, or the clock resets

options.label: Timeout, min 45 / mid 45 / max 0
options.desc: the condition must stay true for the whole delay, or the clock resets

options.label: Timeout, min 0 / mid 45 / max 90
options.desc: the condition must stay true for the whole delay, or the clock resets

options.label: Countdown, min 45 / mid 45 / max 45
options.desc: fires when the delay runs out, even if the condition went false meanwhile

options.label: Countdown, min 30 / mid 45 / max 60
options.desc: fires when the delay runs out, even if the condition went false meanwhile

options.label: No delay
options.desc: all three boxes at 0

items.card: Standing Orders, Countdown vs Timeout: Countdown fires when its delay ends even if the condition went false meanwhile. Timeout fires only if the condition stays true for the whole delay; otherwise the clock resets. min/mid/max are ONE random delay bunched toward mid, so a fixed delay needs all three equal. A max below 0.1 s means no delay at all.
items.rationale: Must hold without a gap = Timeout; exactly 45 s = min, mid and max all 45. A max of 0 means no delay, 30/45/60 and 0/45/90 give a random wait, and Countdown would fire even after the zone emptied.

escape.label: None of these fit
escape.desc: no listed option fits the request

items.request: The mission has two objectives, blowing up the radar truck and clearing East out of the village, each with its own trigger. It must end in victory only once both are done, in whichever order, with no script at all. The radar truck is parked beside a well. How should the two triggers' Type be set?

options.label: Both End #1
options.desc: radar trigger End #1, village trigger End #1

options.label: End #1 and End #2
options.desc: radar trigger End #1, village trigger End #2

options.label: End #1 and None
options.desc: radar trigger End #1, village trigger of type None

options.label: End #1 and Lose
options.desc: radar trigger End #1, village trigger Lose

options.label: Both Switch
options.desc: both triggers of type Switch

options.label: Both None
options.desc: both triggers of type None

options.label: Both Lose
options.desc: both triggers of type Lose

items.card: Standing Orders, trigger types: End #n ends the mission with ending n only when EVERY End #n trigger is active at the same moment; triggers with different End numbers each end the mission on their own (the lowest number wins if several qualify at once). Lose ends the mission as lost and beats every End. Switch moves synced groups past their waypoint. None only runs the trigger's own code.
items.rationale: The same End number acts as AND, so both triggers get End #1. End #1 plus End #2 ends on whichever objective is done first; None or Lose on the village trigger means clearing the village never counts toward the win.

items.request: In my single-player mission, the 'West, Detected by East' alarm over the East base never fires. Every East soldier is created by a script after the start, and no East group exists in the mission file. The alarm must still depend on East actually noticing the player's team, and the base has a tall radio mast. What fixes it?

options.label: Put one East soldier on the map
options.desc: anywhere, even at 0 % probability of presence

options.label: Change it to West, Present
options.desc: fires on real positions inside the area, seen or not

options.label: Set it to Repeatedly
options.desc: the trigger can fire again after switching off

options.label: Enlarge the trigger area
options.desc: double both axes of the ellipse

options.label: Add a 10 s Timeout
options.desc: the condition must hold for 10 s before it fires

options.label: Change it to East, Detected by West
options.desc: fires when West knows of East units in the area

options.label: Change it to Anybody, Detected by East
options.desc: counts units of any side, identified or not, that East knows of

items.card: Standing Orders, Detected by: 'A, Detected by B' fires on side B's shared knowledge of side-A units inside the area (last seen within 100 s). The detecting side must exist: in single-player a side's AI centre is created only when the mission file holds at least one group of that side, checked before any presence roll; without it the trigger stops before its Condition and can never fire. Present counts real positions, seen or not.
items.rationale: In single-player, with no East group in the file East has no AI centre, so any Detected by East trigger can never fire; placing one East unit, even at 0 % presence, creates it. West, Present would fire without anyone noticing the player, and the other changes leave East missing.

items.request: The player should be able to ask for an illumination flare through the radio menu as often as he likes during the mission. The menu entry must read Request flare, not the channel's name. The flares are white. How should the trigger be set?

options.label: Radio Alpha, Repeatedly, Text "Request flare"
options.desc: a repeating radio trigger with its own menu label

options.label: Radio Alpha, Once, Text "Request flare"
options.desc: a one-time radio trigger with its own menu label

options.label: Radio Alpha, Repeatedly, Text "null"
options.desc: a repeating radio trigger whose Text is the word null

options.label: Radio Alpha, Repeatedly, Text empty
options.desc: a repeating radio trigger with no Text

options.label: Radio Alpha, Once, Text empty
options.desc: a one-time radio trigger with no Text

options.label: West, Present, Repeatedly, Text "Request flare"
options.desc: an area trigger that fires while West units are inside it

items.card: Standing Orders, radio triggers: a radio trigger adds an entry to the player's radio menu and fires when called; it never scans its area, and timers do nothing. A Once radio trigger disappears from the menu after use; a Repeatedly one stays and can be called again. The entry shows the trigger's Text, or the channel's default name when the Text is empty; a Text of null hides the entry and blocks the call.
items.rationale: Callable again and again = Repeatedly; a custom label = the Text field. Once vanishes after one call, an empty Text shows the channel name, null hides the entry, and West, Present is not a radio call.

items.card: Doc 43, correlated one-of-N choices: native presence is per object, so it cannot express 'layout A or layout B'. Four lowerings can: A, a stored campaign roll read by presence conditions (SP campaign missions after the bootstrap); B, a roller object whose presence condition rolls once at load (standalone SP, first missions, MP; in MP the server rolls and broadcasts); C, init.sqs pruning (SP only); D, lobby parameters param1/param2, set before objects are created and readable by presence conditions (MP; a 'Random' value resolves through B on the server). Per-unit presence, placement radius and start markers are not correlated.
